question.problem: Given that $v(r,\theta )=r(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta ),$ find $\frac{∂v}{∂y},$ where $(x,y)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta )$ are the corresponding plane polar coordinates.
question.worked_solution:
We will make use of the following chain rule formula:

$$
\frac{∂v}{∂y}=\frac{∂v}{∂r}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\frac{1}{r}\frac{∂v}{∂\theta }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $v$ with respect to $r$ and $\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂v}{∂r}=1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta ,\,\frac{∂v}{∂\theta }=-2r\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Then, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\frac{1}{r}(-2r\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta -2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
